evidence: The ectodomain is shedded from the surface of keratinocytes resulting in a 120-kDa soluble form, also named as 120 kDa linear IgA disease antigen; terminal pLDDT n/a; terminal CA neighbors n/a; stalk n/a
decided_by: l1-cterm-build (delegated by Becca 2026-11-12, "use your best judgment")
reason: The processing is native, so the arm keeps native sequence: a mutated site would put a construct the cell does not make on the surface. A tag before a releasing cut would report the membrane stub, not the protein. At the C-terminus the tag reports the uncut fraction still on the surface; any extracellular tag on these members shares that exposure. ITM2B differs: furin removes only a 23-aa C-terminal peptide and the folded domain stays, so its tag moves before the site
would_change_it: evidence that the surface fraction is undetectable

question: weak C-out call (no_v2)
decision: keep the cassette at the C-terminus
rejected_alternatives: take the member out of the build until its orientation is measured
evidence: DeepTMHMM v1: 1 TM, last helix 19 residues, extracellular tail 217; DeepTMHMM v2: no row, C-terminus no v2 row; UniProt P54709: Extracellular 57-279 (ECO:0000255); UniProt signal peptide none, 1 TM
decided_by: coordinator under Becca's 2026-11-12 delegation and her 2026-11-14 instruction to manage the C-terminal rung
reason: UniProt: Extracellular 57-279 (ECO:0000255). DeepTMHMM v1 is the topology of record, so a C-out call is kept unless an independent source contradicts it. The member is held when (1) UniProt annotates its C-terminus cytoplasmic on experimental evidence (ECO:0000269); (2) UniProt describes a type I protein, with a cleaved signal peptide, one TM helix and a cytoplasmic C-terminus, so that v1's C-out call rests on reading the signal peptide as the only TM helix; (3) the call is weak (a v1 extracellular tail under 5 residues, or DeepTMHMM v2 disagreeing, calling no TM helix or having no row) and UniProt annotates the C-terminus cytoplasmic on any evidence; or (4) v2 puts the C-terminus in the cytoplasm and neither UniProt (an extracellular annotation at this member's C-terminus) nor a curated lane override (lane_overrides.tsv) places it outside. An ortholog with no UniProt entry follows its gene's human member under (1) and (2). A cytoplasmic annotation that is only a sequence-model prediction (ECO:0000255), on a call where v1 and v2 agree and the protein is not type I, is kept and flagged
would_change_it: an independent source placing the C-terminus in the cytoplasm

scope: every L1 insert (shared 2-nt pad after the stop)
question: stop context TAAC (pad CC) or TAAG (pad GC)
decision: keep TAAC (pad CC)
rejected_alternatives: TAAG (pad GC)
evidence: build_constructs.py: pad CC since the 2026-10-01 handle revision
decided_by: l1-cterm-build (delegated by Becca 2026-11-12, "use your best judgment")
reason: TAA is the strongest stop codon either way. CC is the pad of every construct designed and ordered since the 2026-10-01 handle revision, so keeping it keeps L1 comparable with them. The pad is shared by every L1 member, so changing it would change every insert on every rung for a +4 purine effect on termination that we have not measured. The readthrough product would be a short extension through the barcode handle
would_change_it: a readthrough measurement on a tagged construct
